passages.text: INTRODUCTION This section provides management’s discussion of the financial condition, changes in financial condition, and results of operations of Atmos Energy Corporation and its consolidated subsidiaries with specific information on results of operations and liquidity and capital resources. It includes management’s interpretation of our financial results, the factors affecting these results, the major factors expected to affect future operating results, and future investment and financing plans. This discussion should be read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements and notes thereto. Several factors exist that could influence our future financial performance, some of which are described in Item 1A above, “Risk Factors”. They should be considered in connection with evaluating forward-looking statements contained in this report or otherwise made by or on behalf of us since these factors could cause actual results and conditions to differ materially from those set out in such forward-looking statements. Cautionary Statement for the Purposes of the Safe Harbor under the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995 The statements contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K may contain “forward-looking statements” within the meaning of Section 27A of the Securities Act of 1933 and Section 21E of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934. All statements other than statements of historical fact included in this Report are forward-looking statements made in good faith by us and are intended to qualify for the safe harbor from liability established by the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. When used in this Report, or any other of our documents or oral presentations, the words “anticipate”, “believe”, “estimate”, “expect”, “forecast”, “goal”, “intend”, “objective”, “plan”, “projection”, “seek”, “strategy”, or similar words are intended to identify forward-looking statements. Such forward-looking statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied in the statements relating to our strategy, operations, markets, services, rates, recovery of costs, availability of gas supply, and other factors. credit_strengths.text: Operating margin sits well above the utilities sector median and improved year over year, reflecting constructive rate outcomes and cost recovery across the natural gas distribution footprint. This supports stable internal cash generation through the regulatory cycle.

Interest coverage is strong and improved year over year, running far above the sector median, so operating earnings comfortably absorb the disclosed nonoperating interest burden. This headroom is the principal mitigant against the elevated leverage profile.

key_risks.text: Leverage is elevated and drifting upward: gross leverage rose year over year and net leverage also increased, though both remain below the sector median. Headroom to the next risk-band boundary is thin, so a modest EBITDA decline or incremental borrowing would push the profile lower.

The disclosed risk factors center on regulatory and political decisions, pipeline integrity and safety program costs, and inherent hazards of distributing, transporting and storing natural gas. Adverse rate outcomes or integrity spending would pressure recovery timing and cash flow.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Operating cash flow covers dividends comfortably but falls short of capital expenditure plus dividends, and free cash flow is negative, so the capital program is funded partly with new debt. This is typical for a rate-base growth utility but keeps leverage on an upward path.

The maturity ladder is heavily weighted to later years, with only a small near-term repayment and the bulk due after year five, limiting refinancing pressure. Cash on hand is modest relative to debt, so refinancing depends on continued market access.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative financial risk profile is Significant, driven by leverage and cash-flow tiers that sit at the weaker end. Leverage and cash-flow-to-debt both compare favorably with the sector median, but the leverage cushion to the next boundary is narrow.

Our forward view is that coverage and margin strength offset the negative free cash flow and rising debt, provided regulators continue to allow timely cost recovery. A liquidity shortfall is visible in the current ratio, which is below one and slightly weaker year over year, warranting monitoring.

credit_strengths.text: 營運利潤率遠高於公用事業行業中位數，並較去年同期改善，反映天然氣配送業務範圍內有利的費率結果及成本回收。此支撐監管週期內穩定的內部現金產生。
利息覆蓋率強勁並較去年同期改善，遠高於行業中位數，因此營運盈利可輕鬆吸收所披露的非營運利息負擔。此緩衝是應對偏高槓桿狀況的主要緩解因素。

key_risks.text: 槓桿偏高且呈上升趨勢：總槓桿較去年同期上升，淨槓桿亦增加，儘管兩者仍低於行業中位數。距下一風險區間邊界的緩衝薄弱，因此EBITDA小幅下降或增量借款將使狀況進一步下移。
所披露的風險因素集中於監管及政治決策、管道完整性及安全計劃成本，以及配送、運輸及儲存天然氣的固有危險。不利的費率結果或完整性支出將對回收時機及現金流構成壓力。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 營運現金流可輕鬆覆蓋股息，但不足以覆蓋資本支出加股息，且自由現金流為負，因此資本計劃部分以新債務融資。此對費率基礎增長的公用事業而言屬典型情況，但使槓桿維持上升路徑。
到期結構嚴重集中於較後年份，近期還款僅佔小部分，大部分於五年後到期，限制再融資壓力。手頭現金相對債務而言規模適中，因此再融資依賴持續的市場准入。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性財務風險狀況為Significant，由處於較弱端的槓桿及現金流層級所驅動。槓桿及現金流對債務比率均優於行業中位數，但距下一邊界的槓桿緩衝狹窄。
我們的前瞻觀點是，覆蓋率及利潤率強勁可抵銷負自由現金流及上升的債務，前提是監管機構繼續允許及時的成本回收。流動性短缺可見於流動比率，該比率低於一且較去年同期略為轉弱，值得監察。
